issues.title: Cancelling a superseded build reruns the replacing build's steps in BuildKit
issues.description:
Observed on the Y Transfer service (Utils / production) on 2026-09-24 with builder v0.1.85 and BuildKit v0.31/0.32. Three pushes landed within a minute. The build that replaced the cancelled one took 5.5 minutes instead of about 3, because BuildKit killed its compile step with `exit code: 137: context canceled` right as it finished and then ran the whole step again.

## Cause

Two things stack.

**1. Push-triggered builds clone the branch head, not the commit on the deployment.**
`internal/api/handlers/github/webhook.go` stores the push's commit SHA on the deployment but does not set `CHECKOUT_COMMIT_SHA` on the build job. Only `services/deployments/create.go` and `redeploy.go` set it. The builder (`pkg/builder/builders/docker_file.go`) then clones `GIT_REF` and builds whatever the branch points at when the pod runs. In the case above, the build labelled `c84154e` cloned master two seconds after `227c4b6` was pushed and built the same tree as its replacement. This is also a correctness problem: a deployment can claim commit X while the image contains commit Y.

**2. The replacing build starts before the cancelled one is gone.**
`deployctl.go` calls `k8s.CancelJobsByServiceID` (a foreground Job delete that returns immediately) and then `CreateDeployment` right after. The old builder pod kept running for a few seconds. Timeline from the build logs:

* 06:43:27 old build starts `RUN cargo leptos build`
* 06:43:32 old deployment marked cancelled
* 06:43:35 old builder pod gets `context canceled` and exits
* 06:43:35 new build reaches the same `RUN` step
* 06:46:00 shared step ends with `exit code: 137: context canceled`, new build reruns it from scratch
* 06:48:28 rerun finishes

Because the two trees were identical, BuildKit merged the two builds onto one step. `solver/jobs.go` `sharedOp.Exec` does not keep a result from a run that ended with a cancellation, so the surviving caller gets flightcontrol's retry and executes the step again.

## Also noticed

* `pkg/builder/builders/builders.go` `configDigest` includes `SecretsHash`, so the registry cache ref (`<repo>:<digest>-buildcache`) changes whenever a service variable changes. Buildkit already invalidates only the steps that read a changed secret, so keying the whole cache on it throws away every cached layer for one variable edit.
* `registrycache/cleanup.go` `planDeletions` sorts build cache tags first, so crossing the disk threshold deletes every build cache before touching old images. The first Y Transfer cache tag disappeared between two deploys this way.

## Suggested fixes

1. Set `CHECKOUT_COMMIT_SHA` in the webhook path, same as create and redeploy.
2. In `deployctl.go`, wait for the cancelled job's pods to be gone before creating the new job, or skip the cancel when the running build is already on the same commit.
3. Consider dropping `SecretsHash` from `configDigest` for the cache ref, and keeping at least the newest build cache per repo in `protectedTags`.

issues.title: Image pull failures show "Couldn't launch" with no reason anywhere in the UI
issues.description:
## What happened

Tezara Web deployment `2fe65b0c-bde6-4353-8d30-6cf770487a1e` (commit `760f1a3`) built fine, the builder logged `Deployment successful`, then the pod could never start:

```
failed to pull and unpack image "docker-registry.unbind-system:5000/tezara:760f1a3b13d4-f44939710f2e": short read: expected 3849738 bytes but got 0: unexpected EOF
```

The registry had a manifest pointing at a 3.8MB layer but served 0 bytes for it. The pod sat in `ImagePullBackOff`. The old pod kept serving, so the site stayed up.

The UI showed "Couldn't launch" / ERROR and nothing else. No reason on the service card, nothing in the deploy logs tab (the container never started, so there are no logs), and the build logs say it succeeded. The only place the error exists is `replica_events` / the container `state_message` in the API response, which the web app doesn't render.

## Why the reason is missing

**API:** `apps/api/internal/services/deployments/replica_data.go`

* L152 and L172: `ContainerStateImagePullError` only sets `hasPending = true`. Unlike crashing containers, it never adds anything to `crashingReasons`, and nothing sets `StatusMessage`.
* L179–190: the status is still flipped to `launch-error` because there's an `image_pull_back_off` event, so the status says error but both reason fields are empty.
* The full error text is already available: `pod_health.go` L363 puts `container.State.Waiting.Message` into `StateMessage`. It just never reaches `CrashingReasons` / `StatusMessage`.

**Web:** `apps/web/src/components/deployment/panel/tabs/deploy-logs/deploy-logs.tsx`

* L60–64: `getLaunchMessage` only shows `status_message`, then `crashing_reasons`. Both are empty here, so no notice is shown.
* `replica_events` isn't rendered anywhere in the web app.

## Also wrong in the same response

* L217: `ReplicaEvents: append(events, staleEvents...)` mixes the old pod's events into the new deployment. The failed deployment showed the previous pod's `container_stopped ... exit code 139` from 2026-09-14 next to the pull error. That makes it look like the new deployment crashed with a segfault.

## Fix

* In `calculateReplicaData`, when a container is in `ContainerStateImagePullError` (or when an `image_pull_back_off` / `scheduling_failed` / `node_not_ready` event drives the status to `launch-error`), add the container's `StateMessage` (or the event message) to `crashingReasons` or set `StatusMessage`. Then the existing `getLaunchMessage` notice shows it with no web change needed.
* Keep stale events out of the current deployment's `replica_events`, or mark them as belonging to the previous deployment.

## Still unknown: why the registry served an empty layer

I can't see the registry pod or its logs from a team API key, so I couldn't confirm the cause. At the time of the push/pull the node was under heavy memory pressure (29.6 of 30GB at 13:20 UTC, load average 47 at 13:25), and a full registry disk ([UNB-246](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-246/registry-volume-is-4gi-and-the-cleanup-job-is-broken-builds-fail-with)) would produce the same result. Worth checking the `docker-registry` pod's restarts, logs and volume usage around 2026-09-25 13:18–13:28 UTC. Separately, the builder could check that the pushed image can actually be pulled before logging `Deployment successful`.

Retried as deployment `4a792878-8d85-4837-ac12-5a4bc81764f7` with the build cache off.

issues.title: Registry cleanup runs garbage-collect on the live registry and breaks freshly pushed images
issues.description:
## What happened

Tezara Web (commit `760f1a3`) built and pushed fine, then every pull failed:

```
failed to pull and unpack image "docker-registry.unbind-system:5000/tezara:760f1a3b13d4-f44939710f2e": short read: expected 3849738 bytes but got 0: unexpected EOF
```

Rebuilding with build cache disabled produced the same tag and failed the same way. On the registry pod:

* `find /var/lib/registry -name data -size 0` returns nothing, so there are no empty blob files on disk.
* The registry logs have no disk or I/O errors. The only errors are the normal `blob unknown` / `manifest unknown` 404s from BuildKit's existence checks.
* Disk is 17.4G / 19.5G (89%).

So the registry says it has a 3.8MB layer (gives the size) but has no data to serve for it, and a new push doesn't replace it because BuildKit's HEAD check says the layer already exists.

## Cause

`apps/api/internal/infrastructure/registrycache/cleanup.go`: the `registry-cleanup` CronJob runs every hour (`0 * * * *`). When usage is over `MAX_STORAGE`, it deletes manifests and then runs (L384):

```
/bin/registry garbage-collect /etc/distribution/config.yml --delete-untagged=true
```

against the running registry, while builds can be pushing.

1. **Garbage collection on a live registry.** The distribution docs say GC must run with the registry stopped or in read-only mode. The running registry keeps an in-memory blob descriptor cache. When GC deletes blob data the registry still has cached, HEAD keeps returning 200 with the old size (so BuildKit skips the upload), and GET sends the headers and then 0 bytes. That is exactly the error above, and it survives rebuilds until the registry pod restarts.
2. `--delete-untagged` **targets images that were just pushed.** A dry run right after the push (`registry garbage-collect --dry-run --delete-untagged`) listed the layers **and the config blob (**`sha256:7681dfed…`**)** of the tagged `tezara:760f1a3b13d4-f44939710f2e` image as `layer link eligible for deletion`. So even a correctly timed run would unlink images that are tagged and about to be deployed. The likely reason is that BuildKit pushes an OCI index (with attestations) and the child manifest is untagged.
3. **Nothing stops it running during a build.** A push that overlaps the hourly run can lose blobs mid-upload.

## Fix

* Run GC with the registry in read-only mode (`storage.maintenance.readonly.enabled: true`) or scaled to 0, then restart the registry so its blob descriptor cache is cleared.
* Drop `--delete-untagged`. Manifests are already deleted explicitly by tag in `Run()`, so plain `garbage-collect` is enough to free their blobs. If it has to stay, protect OCI index children.
* Don't let the cleanup and builds overlap: skip or postpone the cleanup while a build is pushing, and block builds while GC runs.
* Separately ([UNB-352](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-352/image-pull-failures-show-couldnt-launch-with-no-reason-anywhere-in-the)): the builder logs `Deployment successful` without checking the image can be pulled.

## Workaround used

1. `kubectl -n unbind-system patch cronjob registry-cleanup -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`
2. Restart the registry pod to clear its cache.
3. Redeploy.

Postgres: Slot WAL Keep Size defaults to unlimited, which lets a replication slot fill the volume
issues.description:
## Problem

Slot WAL Keep Size (`maxSlotWalKeepSizeMb`) defaults to `0`, which renders as `max_slot_wal_keep_size: "-1"`: unlimited. With WAL Level set to Logical, a single replication slot can make Postgres keep WAL until the volume is full, even when the database holds almost no data. When the disk fills, Postgres stops and won't start again.

This happened to Ragbag's production Postgres on 2026-09-27. It had to be deleted and recreated.

## Evidence (Lexeme: Zero + Postgres, 2 GB volume)

* The database itself is about 38 MB, but volume usage grew in a straight line by about 33.7 MB/hour, from 274 MB to 978 MB in about 20 hours.
* At 06:05 UTC on 2026-09-27, Slot WAL Keep Size was set to 256 MB. Postgres reloaded its config, with no restart. By the next checkpoint (06:15), usage had dropped to 408 MB and it has stayed there.
* Zero's slot stayed active and wasn't invalidated. Zero didn't reset or re-sync.
* WAL archiving was healthy the whole time (0 failures), so the only thing holding the WAL was the unlimited slot retention.

## Why the default matters on Unbind

Unlimited is Postgres's own default, but it assumes someone is watching the slots. Unbind makes logical replication a one-click option, and the tools that need it (Zero, Electric, Debezium) each create a slot. The default volume is only 1 GiB, and nothing in the UI warns about it. Zero also writes a small WAL message every 30 seconds, which makes Spilo switch to a new 16 MB WAL segment every 30 minutes. At that rate, one slot fills a 1 GiB volume in about a day.

## Proposal

* When `walLevel` is `logical` and `maxSlotWalKeepSizeMb` isn't set, default it to about 25% of the volume size (256 MB on 1 GiB). An explicit value still overrides it.
* Change the field's help text so that "Unlimited" warns that a single replication slot can fill the whole disk.

Relevant files: `apps/api/pkg/databases/assets/definitions/databases/postgres/definition.yaml`, `metadata.yaml`, and the database section of the web settings panel.

comments.body:
One more thing to fix while working on this: Slot WAL Keep Size has no upper limit, in the UI or in the API.

* **Web:** the field only checks for a positive integer (`validateNumberField` in `database-section.tsx`). Replication Slots and WAL Senders stop at 1000, but this field has no `max`. Typing a long number stages it. The input then shows it as `1.234567890123457e+68`, because the staged value goes through `Number()` and back to a string.
* **API:** `MaxSlotWalKeepSizeMB` in `ent/schema/service_config_types.go` has `minimum:"0"` and no `maximum`.
* **Postgres:** `max_slot_wal_keep_size` is an int in MB, so anything above 2147483647 gets rejected when the config loads. Well before that, any value larger than the volume means the same as unlimited, which is the problem this issue is about.

Suggestion: cap the value on both the web and API sides. A limit tied to the volume size would fit with the 25% default proposed above.

issues.title: Support wildcard hosts (*.example.com) and their certificates
issues.description:
## Use case

Compend (Utils project, service `Compend`) serves every published document on its own subdomain, `https://<id>.compend.fyi`, so each document gets its own browser origin, apart from the dashboard at `compend.fyi` and from other documents. Postplan does the same with `<id>.postplan.dev`. This needs one service to answer a wildcard host, `*.compend.fyi`, next to its normal host `compend.fyi`. Any app with per-tenant or per-item subdomains has the same need (user sites, previews, multi-tenant SaaS).

`compend.fyi` is on Cloudflare (proxied, SSL/TLS mode "Full"), so visitors get Cloudflare's free wildcard certificate. Only the hop from Cloudflare to the server needs a certificate for the wildcard.

## What happened

1. **The dashboard won't take the host.** `apps/web/src/lib/helpers/is-domain.ts` requires every label to start with a letter or digit, so `*.compend.fyi` is rejected. The API doesn't validate the host format (`services/service/update.go` only checks collisions), so it was added through the API (MCP `update-service`, `upsert_hosts`).
2. **Routing was built fine.** The operator made an HTTPS listener with hostname `*.compend.fyi` and added it to the HTTPRoute (`resourcebuilder/networking/gateway.go`). Gateway API allows wildcard hostnames.
3. **No certificate could be issued.** The only ClusterIssuer, `letsencrypt-prod`, uses the HTTP-01 challenge, and Let's Encrypt never issues wildcard certificates over HTTP-01. There's no DNS-01 solver.
4. **The wildcard also broke the service's other host.** The operator makes one Certificate per service covering all its hosts (`dnsNames = [compend.fyi, *.compend.fyi]`). The order can never succeed, so the existing secret kept its old Let's Encrypt certificate for `compend.fyi` only. Envoy then reset every TLS handshake for `<id>.compend.fyi`, so Cloudflare showed 525. `compend.fyi` itself would also have stopped renewing at expiry.
5. **Workaround:** deleted the TLS secret by hand (`kubectl -n default-8lthbjcse5pr delete secret compend-djhylzz7uyjh-tls-secret`). cert-manager then created its temporary self-signed certificate (`issue-temporary-certificate`), covering both names, issuer `cert-manager.local`. Envoy serves it, Cloudflare "Full" accepts it, and documents now open. The ACME order keeps failing and retrying in the background indefinitely.

## What's wrong in the UI now

* **"Certificate pending" forever, though nothing is pending.** `dns_discovery.go` → `certificateCoversHost` treats any certificate issued by `cert-manager.local` as not issued. Both hosts therefore stay `tls_status: attempting`, and `service-url.tsx` shows "Issuing the certificate… This can take a few minutes" permanently. This covers `compend.fyi` too, even though it serves fine.
* `*.compend.fyi` **is shown as a normal, clickable domain.** "Visit" opens `https://*.compend.fyi`, which isn't a real hostname. A wildcard should read as a pattern ("any subdomain of [compend.fyi](<http://compend.fyi>)"), not a link.
* **A wildcard deploy showed "Launching" while pods were green.** Saving the host queued a redeploy of the same image that was already running. No new pod started, so it never got a `container_started` event and sat on "Launching" until a newer deployment replaced it (then it became `removed`). A redeploy that reuses the running image should go straight to active.

## How Unbind could solve it

**1. Accept wildcard hosts deliberately**

* Allow a leading `*.` in `is-domain.ts` and in the API (with validation: one leading label only, not `*.com`).
* In the UI, show wildcard hosts as a pattern with no "Visit" button (or a "Visit an example" that fills in a sample label). The DNS check should look for the `*` record.
* Treat a wildcard and its apex as separate hosts for collision checks, and warn when two services' wildcards overlap.

**2. One Certificate per host, not one per service.** A host that can't get a certificate should never block the service's other hosts. Right now one wildcard stops `compend.fyi` from renewing.

**3. Pick how each host gets its certificate** (per host, or per service):

* **Let's Encrypt, HTTP-01** (today's default). Not allowed for wildcards.
* **Let's Encrypt, DNS-01.** A team or instance setting holds a DNS provider token (start with Cloudflare, which cert-manager supports out of the box). The operator uses a DNS-01 ClusterIssuer or a solver `selector.dnsZones` for that zone. It must be managed by Unbind itself: a hand-patched `letsencrypt-prod` gets overwritten by the helmfile hook on the next upgrade. This is the proper fix for wildcards.
* **Proxy handles TLS / self-signed at the origin**, the toggle case for hosts behind Cloudflare in "Full" mode. The operator creates a self-signed certificate directly (a cert-manager `SelfSigned` issuer) with no ACME order, and the UI shows something like "Self-signed (TLS handled by Cloudflare)" as a final state, not "pending". It works today with no token, but it's not compatible with Cloudflare "Full (strict)", and the UI should say so.
* Optionally, **bring your own certificate**, e.g. a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate (free, 15 years, covers `*.compend.fyi`), stored as a secret the operator doesn't overwrite.

**4. Report the certificate status truthfully**

* `certificateCoversHost` shouldn't turn "self-signed on purpose" into "attempting" forever. It should distinguish issued (ACME), self-signed (chosen) and pending (an order in progress), and failing (the order errors, with the reason from cert-manager's Order/Challenge, e.g. "Let's Encrypt can't issue wildcard certificates with HTTP-01").
* For a wildcard with only HTTP-01 available, the UI should say up front what's needed (DNS-01 or proxy-handled TLS) instead of showing a spinner.

## Current state for Compend

* The service hosts are `compend.fyi` and `*.compend.fyi`. Their TLS is cert-manager's temporary self-signed certificate (after the secret was deleted by hand), and Cloudflare "Full" is set on the zone.
* The dashboard shows both hosts as "Issuing the certificate" permanently.
* The ACME order for the Certificate keeps failing in the background.
* If the Certificate is ever reissued (for example, a host is added or removed), the secret has to be deleted again or the wildcard breaks. Option 3 (DNS-01 or proxy-handled TLS) removes the need for that.

issues.title: Domain routing: redirects, basic auth, headers, path sharing and external upstreams
issues.description:
Domains only route a host to one service. Moving the banano and appditto sites onto Unbind needed a per-team nginx `edge` service for everything else.

## Cases from the banano migration

* www to apex 308: [natrium.io](<http://natrium.io>), [appditto.com](<http://appditto.com>), [nanopaperwallet.com](<http://nanopaperwallet.com>)
* Redirects: [plugins.danklinux.com](<http://plugins.danklinux.com>) 301 to [danklinux.com/plugins](<http://danklinux.com/plugins>), [danklinux.com/blog/v1.2-release](<http://danklinux.com/blog/v1.2-release>) 301 to /blog/v1-2-release
* Basic auth: [invoice.appditto.com](<http://invoice.appditto.com>)
* Several services on one domain: [appditto.com](<http://appditto.com>) serves the frontend on `/` and the contact server on `/inquire`
* External upstream: [install.danklinux.com](<http://install.danklinux.com>) proxies DankMaterialShell's [install.sh](<http://install.sh>) from [raw.githubusercontent.com](<http://raw.githubusercontent.com>). Users pipe it to `sh`, so a redirect is not a safe substitute
* Response headers: [api.danklinux.com](<http://api.danklinux.com>) sent `Cache-Control: public, max-age=600`
* Real client IP behind Cloudflare: old ingresses used `real_ip_header CF-Connecting-IP`, and the appditto contact form rate-limits on `X-Forwarded-For`

## Why it doesn't work today

* No redirect, auth or header options on a domain
* One service per domain: `CountHostConflicts` matches the host and ignores the path (apps/api/internal/services/service create.go, update.go, apply_staged_changes.go), and the gateway provider builds one listener per host per service (apps/operator/internal/resourcebuilder/networking/gateway.go)

## Proposal

Envoy first. nginx and traefik have annotations and middlewares for the same things.

1. Redirects on a domain: target URL, status 301/302/307/308, keep the path or not, with www to apex as a shortcut. Gateway API `RequestRedirect` filter
2. Basic auth on a domain from a variable holding htpasswd lines. Envoy Gateway `SecurityPolicy` `basicAuth`
3. Response header modifiers on a domain. Gateway API `ResponseHeaderModifier`
4. Trusted proxy and client IP header as a system setting, applied with `ClientTrafficPolicy` so `X-Forwarded-For` carries the real client IP
5. Path sharing: allow a domain on several services when their paths differ. One listener per domain, one HTTPRoute per service matched on path. Biggest change, needs a design
6. External upstream as a domain target (Envoy `Backend`)

1 to 4 are small and remove most of the edge configs. 5 and 6 can follow.

## Workaround in use

A per-team nginx `edge` service, with its config in a variable mounted as a file (dux/danklinux, appditto/edge).

attachments.subtitle: master

comments.body:
**Done (in review, not merged)**
- One HTTPRoute per domain, bound to its own listener. Before, domains of one service shared a route, and per the Gateway API tie-break rules every domain could land on the first one's port.
- Redirect per domain: URL plus 301/302/307/308, default 308. A URL without a path keeps the request path, one with a path replaces it. Covers www to apex and plugins. to danklinux.com/plugins.
- Basic auth per domain: username and password typed in the UI. The API keeps a SHA hash, the only format Envoy Gateway reads, and never returns it. No variable mount, so no ordering problem.
- Response headers per domain, as Name: value. Covers the api. Cache-Control and the HSTS gap.
- Client IP header per service, under Networking. Empty is automatic: CF-Connecting-IP while a domain is proxied through Cloudflare. Envoy then takes the visitor's address from it and passes X-Forwarded-For on as Cloudflare sent it, so the contact server's rate limit sees the visitor. Envoy Gateway installs only.
- Same options on ingress-nginx (annotations and a configuration snippet) and Traefik (middlewares). Unit tested only, not run against a live nginx or Traefik.
- Release: deploy/releases/v0.1.101 has the Service CRD and the operator ClusterRole with securitypolicies and clienttrafficpolicies. The builder image has to ship with it, since an older builder drops the new fields on a build deploy.

**Not done**
- 5, several services on one domain by path. appditto.com / and /inquire still need the edge.
- 6, external upstream. install.danklinux.com still needs the edge.
- Redirects are per domain, not per path. danklinux.com/blog/v1.2-release and the .well-known files still need the edge.
- No HSTS default, it is a header per domain.
- A redirect-only domain still sits on a service and gets a certificate. Plain HTTP still only answers ACME.
- The automatic client IP header is picked at deploy time. A domain moving onto Cloudflare is picked up on the next deploy.

**Edge after this lands**
- appditto/edge: drop the three www redirects and the invoice basic auth. Keep it for the appditto.com path split.
- dux/danklinux edge: drop the plugins redirect and the api. headers. Keep it for the blog redirect, .well-known and install.sh.

**Notes**
- The basic auth hash is unsalted SHA1. Fine as a gate, not a credential store.
- ingress-nginx only takes the snippet with annotations-risk-level Critical, which the chart already sets.
- Verified on k3d with Envoy Gateway: redirects, basic auth 401/200, headers, and the client IP policy being set and removed.

Found another one while moving umami.danklinux.com: HSTS.

ingress-nginx adds `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` to TLS hosts by default, and the old origin sent it (checked with `--resolve` against the old LB). Unbind on Envoy sends no HSTS, so a move from ingress-nginx silently drops it. Browsers that already cached it keep it for up to a year.

This fits the response header proposal: an HSTS toggle per domain, or a system default, set on the HTTPRoute with a `ResponseHeaderModifier` filter. Cloudflare's zone-level HSTS setting works around it for proxied domains.

Edge workarounds in place on the banano cluster, to replace once this lands.

**dux / danklinux `edge`** (hosts danklinux.com, plugins., install., api.)
- `.well-known/org.flathub.VerifiedApps.txt` and `microsoft-identity-association.json` returned inline. Could move to static files in the docs repo instead
- `/blog/v1.2-release` 301 to `/blog/v1-2-release`, plugins. 301 to danklinux.com/plugins (needs item 1)
- install. proxies install.sh from raw.githubusercontent.com with TLS verification (needs item 6)
- api. adds `Cache-Control` and sets `X-Real-IP`/`X-Forwarded-For` from `CF-Connecting-IP` (items 3 and 4). The app could do both itself

**appditto / `edge`** (hosts appditto.com, www.appditto.com, www.natrium.io, www.nanopaperwallet.com, invoice.appditto.com)
- 3 www to apex 308s keeping the path (item 1). A "www alias" option on a domain would cover all three
- appditto.com `/` to frontend, `/inquire` to the contact server (item 5). The contact server rate-limits by `X-Forwarded-For`, so the edge sets it from `CF-Connecting-IP` (item 4)
- invoice. basic auth from an htpasswd variable mounted as a file (item 2)

**Seen along the way**
- Services that get their domain directly (natrium.io, nanopaperwallet.com) see the Hetzner LB as the client IP, which the old ingress fixed with `real_ip_header CF-Connecting-IP`. Item 4 as a system setting covers everyone at once
- A variable mount for a key that doesn't exist yet blocks the pod from starting, so an edge with a credential mount (htpasswd) can't deploy until the secret is filled in. Native basic auth on a domain avoids that ordering problem
- Plain HTTP on port 80 only serves ACME challenges, so redirect-only hosts still need TLS and a backing service today

issues.title: banano: move banano-node and nano-node into the new project network
issues.description:
banano-node (cax31) and nano-node (cax41) are Cloud servers in the old Hetzner project on network `banano-k3s`. The new Unbind cluster is in its own project, so for now it reaches them over their public IPs through the `nano-nodes` Cloud Firewall: TCP 7072, 7074, 17076, 7076 and 7078, open to the 3 cluster node IPs (188.245.26.212, 2.31.9.171, 2.31.8.222). Pods leave through their node's public IPv4, which I checked.

That setup is temporary:

* RPC and websocket traffic crosses the public network unencrypted.
* The allowlist breaks when a cluster node is replaced and gets a new IP.
* Every pod on the cluster, from any team, can reach node RPC.

## Ports in use

| server | old private IP | public IP | RPC | WS | other |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| banano-node | 10.4.0.1 | 188.245.66.133 | 7072 | 7074 | work server 17076 |
| nano-node | 10.7.0.1 | 168.119.165.219 | 7076 | 7078 |  |

Used by pippin, betsy, kalium, natrium, natricon, boompow and wban (all 5 chains plus wban-pippin).

## Plan

* Create replacement servers in the new project in nbg1, attached to network `unbind` (10.0.0.0/16), in a free subnet. Avoid 10.0.64.0/18 (nodes), 10.0.96.0/19 (services) and 10.0.128.0/17 (pods).
* Copy the ledgers, then start the nodes and the work server listening on the private IP.
* Point the services at the private IPs. If they read node URLs from team variables, that's one edit per team.
* Remove the firewall rules and delete the old servers. After that the old project has nothing left once the old cluster is gone.

Pod traffic to 10.0.0.0/16 is not masqueraded, because Cilium's native routing CIDR is 10.0.0.0/16. The `unbind` network already has routes for the pod CIDRs, so private servers can reply to pod IPs directly.

issues.title: Email alerts
issues.description:
Unbind can send mail through an SMTP relay now (System > Settings > Email), but it only sends invitations, team-add notices and the test message. Use the relay for alerts too, so problems reach people who aren't watching the UI or a webhook channel.

## Events worth an email

From the existing webhook events (`apps/api/ent/schema/webhook_enums.go`):

* `deployment.failed`

Not events yet, would need new sources:

* Service crashing or crash looping (the deployment `crashing` status and `crashing_reasons` already exist).
* Database backup failed, or no successful backup within the schedule.
* Volume nearly full.
* Certificate failed to issue or renew.
* Node under memory or disk pressure.
* A new Unbind release is available (system admins only).

## Shape

* Opt in per user, scoped to a team or project, with a choice of events. Default off, so turning on SMTP doesn't start mailing everyone.
* Send only to members who can see the resource.
* Dedupe and rate limit: a crash looping service sends one mail, then a reminder or a recovered notice, not one per restart.
* Each mail links straight to the deployment or service in the UI, plus a link to change preferences.
* Send through `EmailService.Send` (`apps/api/internal/services/email/email.go`). If SMTP isn't configured, the settings say so and nothing is queued.

## Open questions

* Should the new event sources also become webhook events, so webhooks and email share one pipeline?
* One digest per incident, or per event?

issues.title: docs: SMTP setup guide with provider recommendations
issues.description:
`apps/docs/content/operations/email.mdx` explains the settings fields and lists providers (Postmark, Resend, SES, Mailgun, SendGrid, Workspace/365), but doesn't recommend one or show how to set any of them up. It matters more once email alerts land ([UNB-377](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-377/email-alerts)).

## Add

* A short recommendation. Resend or Postmark for the least setup, Amazon SES for the lowest cost at volume. Check current pricing and terms while writing; don't copy numbers in from memory.
* One walkthrough per recommended provider: verify the sending domain, add its DNS records, create SMTP credentials, then the exact Host, Port, Username and Encryption to enter in Unbind. Check every value against the provider's docs. Things to cover:
  * Amazon SES: SMTP credentials are not IAM access keys, they have to be generated separately. New accounts start in the sandbox and can only send to verified addresses until production access is granted.
  * Resend and Postmark use an API token as the SMTP password. Note what goes in Username.
* Blocked ports. Some hosts block outgoing SMTP ports; Hetzner Cloud blocks 25 and 465 by default, per their FAQ (confirm while writing). Recommend 587 with STARTTLS, and mention providers' alternate ports where they offer them.
* Troubleshooting, mapped to what **Send Test Email** shows: authentication failed, a timeout (usually a blocked port), a TLS mismatch (465 TLS vs 587 STARTTLS), and the from address on an unverified domain.
* SPF, DKIM and DMARC: one concrete set of example records instead of just naming them.
* Links to this page from the install docs and from Members (invitations).

comments.body: Measured on the banano cluster (Hetzner Cloud, nbg1, 2026-10-13): outbound TCP to 465 and 587 is open for smtp.resend.com, smtp.mx.cloudflare.net and email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, and 2587 to Resend too. So at least on this project 465 isn't blocked. Port 25 wasn't tested. Check the "Hetzner blocks 465" line against Hetzner's current FAQ before writing it into the docs.

issues.title: Health check and variable mount changes never reach a running service
issues.description:
Changing a running service's health check or variable mounts saves the new value, starts a redeploy, and leaves the old value on the Service CR and the pods.

## Repro (banano, 2026-10-13)

1. A git service deployed with an http health check on `/sping`.
2. `update-service` with `health_check: {type: none}`, later `{type: exec, command: "true"}`. `get-service` shows the new value.
3. The redeploy's pods still carry the `/sping` startup, readiness and liveness probes, and the Service CR still has `type: http`.
4. Only a full `trigger-deployment` (rebuild) applied the new check.

## Cause

A config change on a running service redeploys through `CreateCRDFromService` (`apps/api/internal/services/deployments/redeploy.go`). It copies the previous deployment's CR spec, then calls `service_repo.ApplyRuntimeConfig` (`apps/api/internal/repositories/service/runtime_config.go`). That function sets hosts, ports, public, body size, session affinity, replicas, volumes and resources, but not `HealthCheck` or `VariableMounts`. The full build path (`deployctl.go`, `SERVICE_HEALTH_CHECK` / `SERVICE_VARIABLE_MOUNTS`) does pass them.

The change detection in `apps/api/internal/repositories/service/queries.go` compares both fields, so a redeploy is triggered, but it deploys the old values.

## Fix

Set `spec.HealthCheck` (nil for none) and `spec.VariableMounts` in `ApplyRuntimeConfig`. Add a test that a health check change and removal reach the redeploy CR. Also check for other CR fields the redeploy copies forward without updating.

Same class of bug as [UNB-263](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-263/assigning-a-backup-bucket-to-a-deployed-database-never-reaches-the) (backup bucket never reached the cluster).

attachments.subtitle: master

issues.title: Non-root images can't write to a fresh volume
issues.description:
A new volume's root directory is `root:root 755`, and Unbind sets no pod `fsGroup`. An image that runs as a non-root user can read the mount but can't create files in it.

## Seen (banano, 2026-10-12)

ooye (out-of-your-element, runs as uid 10001) with its data volume at `/srv/ooye` failed with `SqliteError: attempt to write a readonly database` (`SQLITE_READONLY_DIRECTORY`). SQLite needs to create journal files next to `ooye.db`. The old cluster had `securityContext.fsGroup: 10001` on the pod.

Worked around with a one-off pod on the same node: `chown 10001:10001 /srv/ooye && chmod 2775`. That only holds until the volume is recreated.

The operator already passes a container `SecurityContext` from the CR (`apps/operator/internal/resourcebuilder/deployment.go`), but there is no pod-level one and no setting in the UI or API.

## Options

* A run-as user / fsGroup setting on the service, applied as the pod `fsGroup` (with `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`).
* Read the image's `USER` at deploy time and use its uid/gid as the default `fsGroup` when the service has a volume.
* An init step that chowns the volume root to the image user on first mount.

Synapse didn't hit this: its entrypoint starts as root and drops to uid 991 after fixing ownership.

issues.title: No way to stop a service without deleting it
issues.description:
Replicas have a minimum of 1, and there is no stop or maintenance switch. Anything that needs the app fully off cannot be done with Unbind's own controls: restoring its database, a migration that must not overlap with the old version, or pausing a misbehaving service.

## Seen (banano, 2026-10-13)

Moving a NodeBB forum: its entrypoint runs `nodebb setup` when it finds an incomplete database, so it must not start while a 4 GB restore is in progress. The forum's README also told you to scale to 0 before NodeBB core upgrades (`kubectl scale --replicas=0`), so schema migrations don't run while the old pod still serves.

Workaround: set the run command to `sleep infinity` and the health check to exec `true`, which replaces the app with a sleeping container. This needed a full rebuild because of the health check redeploy bug.

## Proposal

A Stop / Start action on a service: scale the Deployment to 0 and keep it there, with the service shown as stopped. Optionally a maintenance page on its domains while stopped. Databases may want the same thing.

issues.title: Private and external registries: pull credentials for image services, push targets per team
issues.description:
Image services can only pull public images. The docs say so (`services/deploy-a-docker-image.mdx`: "There is no place in the UI yet to add credentials for a private registry"). There is a system registry backend (`apps/api/internal/services/system/registry_*.go`, a pull secret per registry), but nothing lets an image service use it.

## Seen (banano, 2026-10-13)

thebrownsboard's CI pushed a private `ghcr.io/bbedward/thebrownsboard` image, and the old cluster pulled it with an `imagePullSecret`. On Unbind it had to become a git service, which happens to be what the user wanted. A private image with no repo access (a vendor's registry, or a build from another CI) has no way in.

## Proposal

Registry credentials per team (host, username, token), stored as a dockerconfigjson secret in the team namespace and attached as `imagePullSecrets` to image services whose image host matches. Test the credentials on save, like S3 buckets do.

## Extend: external registry as the build target, per team

What exists today (checked in code, 2026-10-13):

* Builds push to the install's **default registry**. `deployctl.go` calls `GetDefaultRegistry()` and passes its host plus the credentials from its secret in the system namespace (`CONTAINER_REGISTRY_HOST/USER/PASSWORD`) to every build job. `SetDefaultRegistry` and `CreateRegistry` (`internal/services/system/registry_*.go`, which tests the credentials and creates a pull secret) exist, so an install can probably point all builds at GHCR or Docker Hub today. Whether every team namespace also gets the matching pull secret is unverified.
* The operator already supports `Spec.ImagePullSecrets` on the Service CR (`resourcebuilder/deployment.go` `buildImagePullSecrets`), so the plumbing for pull secrets is there.
* Nothing is per team: there is one default registry for the whole install.

Per-team push targets would let each team push to its own org's registry (BananoCoin, appditto, AvengeMedia each need their own write token).

What an external target gains:

* No in-cluster registry volume, garbage collection or cleanup jobs, which have caused bugs ([UNB-246](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-246/registry-volume-is-4gi-and-the-cleanup-job-is-broken-builds-fail-with), [UNB-353](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-353/nothing-tells-us-that-the-registry-is-getting-full-or-needs-to-be), [UNB-354](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-354/registry-cleanup-runs-garbage-collect-on-the-live-registry-and-breaks)).
* Images survive a cluster rebuild and can be shared between clusters.
* No node mirror config (`registries.yaml`, Talos `machine.registries.mirrors`) and no `registryClusterIP` override.

What it costs:

* Public images expose app code and anything baked in at build time. Private ones need a pull secret in every namespace that runs them.
* Every build uploads over the internet and every node pulls over it, so registry outages and rate limits block deploys and restarts.

Related: on ARM-only clusters, existing amd64-only images (e.g. old Docker Hub images) can't run at all. Pull credentials alone don't help there; they have to be rebuilt from source.

comments.body:
## Direction (2026-10-14)

Push targets at three levels. Each one overrides the level above it:

* **Service**: optional override, e.g. publish one service's image to `ghcr.io/<org>/<name>`.
* **Project or team**: default target for every build in it. Overrides the system default registry.
* **System**: the default registry, same as today.

Order: service, then project, then team, then system default.

## What exists (checked in code, 2026-10-14)

* Registries are system wide only. `ent/schema/registry.go` has host, secret name, `is_default` and `insecure`, with no team or project. Builds always use `GetDefaultRegistry()` (`deployctl.go`).
* Every registry's pull secret is copied into every team namespace, both when the registry is created (`registry_create.go`) and when a team is created (`team/create.go` `copyRegistrySecrets`). Every build gets all of them in `IMAGE_PULL_SECRETS`. That settles the "unverified" point in the description.
* The pushed ref is `<host>/<repo name>:<input digest>` (`builders.go` `imageRepository`), and the repo name has no owner in it. GHCR wants `ghcr.io/<owner>/<image>`, so a target needs an owner/org path as well as a host. Nobody has tested whether saving the host as `ghcr.io/<owner>` already works end to end. Buildkit auth uses the saved host as is (`buildkit.go`).
* The build cache ref (`<repo>:<digest>-buildcache`) goes to the same repository, so an external target would get cache tags next to the image.

## Design notes

* Team and project targets have to stay inside that team. System registries get copied into every team namespace, but a team's credentials must not be. Store them only in the team namespace, and only let a service or project pick targets from its own team.
* If the image is private, the service needs the pull secret for the registry it was pushed to. The operator already takes `Spec.ImagePullSecrets`.

## Open questions

* Do we need both team and project defaults, or just one?
* Tags: today the tag is an input digest. Publishing usually also wants `latest` and/or the commit SHA.
* Who can add team registry credentials, and who can pick a target on a service.
* When a target changes, does the service rebuild right away or wait for the next build?
* Image visibility (public/private). Leaning toward out of scope. The OCI distribution spec only covers pull, push, content discovery and content management, so visibility is a per-provider setting (GHCR package settings, Docker Hub repo settings). Managing it would mean provider-specific API calls, and we haven't checked that every provider has an API for it. Push with the provider's default, document that, and let the user change it at the provider. We haven't checked yet what GHCR and Docker Hub default a new image to.

issues.title: MySQL createdb Job is deleted and recreated in a tight loop
issues.description:
A new MySQL service's `<name>-createdb-moco` Job never gets to run. The operator deletes and recreates it about once a second, so its pods are killed before the script finishes, and the loop never ends on its own.

## Seen (banano, 2026-10-13)

MySQL from the Ghost template (`mysql-ld3k8m5lyopo`, MOCO, 8.4.10) in `default-j7hk1yzj82w9`. Over 740 `SuccessfulCreate` events for `job/mysql-ld3k8m5lyopo-createdb-moco` in about 10 minutes, pods always `Terminating` within 1-2s. The database itself works (the `moco` DB exists, Ghost connects), so it's pure churn on the API server, scheduler and kubelet.

Operator log on every pass:

```
Reconciling Job
Deleting existing Job to recreate with new configuration
Waiting for Job to be deleted
Creating new Job with updated configuration
```

## Where

`reconcileJob` in `apps/operator/internal/controller/dependents.go` deletes the Job when `jobFinished` is false and `equality.Semantic.DeepDerivative(desired.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers, existing...)` is false. The comparison came in with `7fc77f5b` (operator: hash rendered specs to skip no-op updates on reconcile).

The live Job's container matches the rendered template from `apps/api/pkg/databases/assets/definitions/databases/mysql/definition.yaml` plus normal API defaults (imagePullPolicy, probe thresholds, terminationMessage\*), which `DeepDerivative` should ignore. So the cause is unconfirmed. Things to check:

* Whether two renders of the same definition differ (args, env, version) and fight each other.
* Whether the Get after the 10 one-second waits returns a Job that is still being deleted, or whether recreating triggers a reconcile that sees the old object.
* Whether the Job's own create/delete events re-enqueue the Service, making the loop self-sustaining once one compare fails.

A unit test that renders the Job twice and runs the same comparison against an API-defaulted copy would pin it down.

issues.title: No network isolation between teams
issues.description:
Unbind creates no NetworkPolicies, so every pod can open connections to every service in every team namespace. Team boundaries exist in RBAC and the UI but not on the network. On the banano install, `kubectl get networkpolicy -A` returns nothing. The operator chart's `allow-metrics-traffic` policy is the only one in the repo.

## Why it matters (banano, 2026-10-12)

On the old cluster (also flat), an attacker got code execution in a Ghost blog pod (CVE-2026-29053) and used it to reach services that had nothing to do with the blog:

* An unauthenticated wallet RPC (pippin, `:11338`): probed `send`, `wallet_export` and `account_create`.
* A shared Redis with no password: read every DB.
* Two Postgres clusters belonging to a bot: about 6,300 connection attempts.
* The Kubernetes API.

None of that would have been reachable if the blog's namespace could only talk to its own services. On Unbind the same thing applies across teams: a compromised service in one team can reach any other team's services, including apps that rely on "only the cluster can reach me" (wallet RPCs, admin ports, metrics endpoints).

## Proposal

Per team namespace, a default policy:

* Ingress allowed from the same namespace, from `unbind-system` (gateway/Envoy, API, registry), and from monitoring (metrics scraping).
* Ingress from other team namespaces denied.
* Optionally a per-service "reachable from other teams" toggle, or per-project isolation inside a team.

Cilium (which the hcloud Talos install uses) enforces standard NetworkPolicy, and k3s ships a NetworkPolicy controller. Check that databases' operator traffic (zalando, MOCO, Altinity), builds (buildkit to the registry) and backups (egress to S3) keep working, and that egress stays open by default.

comments.body:
**Banano after the migration (2026-10-14)**

* The banano Ghost (`ghost-ysnh1o8dg8hb`) runs in the banano team namespace (`default-j7hk1yzj82w9`) next to pippin-banano and pippin-nano. A per-team policy would not have blocked the Ghost to pippin path from the incident above. That needs isolation per project inside a team, or the blog in its own team.
* Cross-team traffic exists: natricon's server (appditto team) calls pippin-nano in the banano team, from its run command (`-rpc-url http://pippin-nano-7eqnbga0944j.default-j7hk1yzj82w9.svc.cluster.local:11338`). A deny-by-default team policy breaks natricon unless that path is allowed.
* wban got its own pippin in the wban team so the five wban-apis do not use the banano pippins. The old cluster had a NetworkPolicy around wban's pippin. Unbind has nothing equivalent, so any pod in any team can reach it and the banano pippins.

**After the change**

* Pods in wban, yekta, dux, bbedward and appditto can no longer reach the banano pippins, Postgres or Redis. natricon's server keeps its access through an explicit allow.
* With per-project isolation, the banano blog could not reach the wallet services in its own team either.

Cross-team traffic the isolation design has to allow, from the banano wallet migration (2026-10-13). Placement: pippin, betsy and kalium in the banano team, natricon and natrium in appditto.

- natricon (appditto) calls pippin-nano (banano) over its RPC.
- betsy (banano) posts node callbacks to natrium-server (appditto). Kalium moves into banano, so betsy to kalium stays in one team.
- pippin RPC has no auth, and the old cluster showed what that costs: the compromised Ghost pod sent about 54k requests to both pippins (Oct 11 to 13). Pippin should only accept its known callers, same team or explicitly allowed cross team.

So per-team default deny needs an explicit allow rule from one service to another service in a different team (natricon to pippin-nano, betsy to natrium-server), not just same-team traffic. Until this lands, these work because nothing blocks cross-team traffic.

issues.title: Scheduled jobs (cron)
issues.description:
Unbind has no way to run something on a schedule. A service is always a long-running Deployment, and the only cron expressions in the product are database backup schedules (`service_config.backup_schedule`) and the internal registry cleanup.

## Seen (banano, 2026-10-13)

The old cluster runs 19 Kubernetes CronJobs that have no home on Unbind, among them:

| job | schedule | what it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| pippin receive-all (banano, nano) | every 10 min | pockets incoming wallet funds |
| boompow moneybags, moneybags-rpc-send | daily, every 3 h | pays out workers |
| kalium-prices, natrium-prices | every 5 min | refreshes wallet price feeds |
| beatrice-ves-price | hourly | price update |
| wban hot-wallet-monitor, total-supply-monitor (x5 chains) | daily, every 5 min | bridge monitoring and alerts |
| thebrownsboard-backup | daily | pg_dump to R2 (replaced by Unbind backups) |

The workarounds are poor: a long-running service with an in-process scheduler (changes the app), or a sidecar loop with `sleep` (no history, no alerts, restarts reset the timing).

## Proposal

A "Cron job" service type (or a schedule on any image or git service) that becomes a Kubernetes CronJob:

* Cron expression with timezone, plus concurrency policy (Forbid by default) and starting deadline.
* Same image, build, variables, references and variable mounts as a normal service. Often it is the app's own image with a different run command, so allow "run this command from service X's image".
* Run history in the UI (last N runs, status, duration, logs), and a "Run now" button.
* Failed runs feed the deployment-failed style alerts ([UNB-377](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-377/email-alerts)).
* MCP tools: create/update the schedule, trigger a run, list runs.

On the operator side: a CronJob built from the Service CR the same way the Deployment is, with history limits set so finished pods don't pile up.

issues.title: System admin: workload health across all teams
issues.description:
The system pages show servers (with a node health section), metrics, settings and updates, but nothing about the workloads running on the install. An admin has to open every team and project, or use kubectl, to find out what's broken.

## What it should show

One page under /system listing problems across every team, most severe first, each linking to the team/project/service:

* **Services:** crashing or crash looping, launch errors, image pull failures, pods pending (unschedulable, volume not attaching), rollouts that never finish, high restart counts.
* **Databases:** last successful backup per database and backup failures. Databases with no backup bucket attached.
* **Domains:** certificates not ready, and how long they've been pending.
* **Volumes:** nearly full, pending, or detached from their service.
* **Platform:** health of `unbind-system` components (Envoy, registry, buildkit, the Unbind operator, cert-manager, the database operators) and Jobs failing or being recreated.

Plus a compact summary on the system overview (counts per category) so problems are visible without opening the page.

## Seen during the banano migration (2026-10-12/13), none visible in the UI

* A MySQL `createdb` Job recreated about once a second for 10+ minutes ([UNB-383](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-383/mysql-createdb-job-is-deleted-and-recreated-in-a-tight-loop)).
* A certificate pending for \~30 minutes because the upstream DNS cached a missing record.
* A Ghost pod crash looping on a stuck migration lock after an interrupted rollout.
* A rollout stalled because the new pod's readiness probe could never pass ([UNB-379](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-379/health-check-and-variable-mount-changes-never-reach-a-running-service)), leaving the old pod serving.
* A team backup bucket that stayed empty because no database had it attached yet.

These are the same signals email alerts ([UNB-377](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-377/email-alerts)) and the notification center ([UNB-355](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-355/notification-center-in-the-ui-and-the-system-for-it-in-the-backend)) need, so the page could share their event sources.

comments.body:
**Also seen 2026-10-14**

* wban-api restarted whenever someone hit `/prices` while CoinEx answered 503 (an async error in an Express 4 route is an unhandled rejection on Node 16). Five bridges holding hot wallets restarted on visitor traffic. It was found in the logs during the cutover, not from the UI.

**After the change**

The /system page lists services restarting across teams, so a crash like this shows up the day it starts instead of being found by reading logs.

issues.title: Docs: Talos hcloud VIP drains the Hetzner API budget, CSI and CCM stop working
issues.description:
On a Talos cluster built with the hcloud-k8s terraform module, the default private control plane VIP (`HCloudVIPConfig`) makes Talos machined call the Hetzner API on every network link change on every node. `network.OperatorVIPConfigController` has `LinkStatus` as an input and runs `GetNetworkAndDeviceIDs` (GET /servers/{id} and GET /networks/{id}, no caching) on each reconcile. Same code on Talos main.

Any pod churn (pod veths, and the Cilium WireGuard interface which updates as pods come and go) turns into API calls. Hetzner limits are per project (3600/h, refill 1/s), so once the budget hits 0 the controller retries about every 0.6s and it never recovers. The hcloud CSI driver and CCM share that budget, so volume create, attach and detach fail with rate_limit_exceeded until the churn stops.

Seen on the banano cluster on 2026-10-13. Churn came from [UNB-383](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-383/mysql-createdb-job-is-deleted-and-recreated-in-a-tight-loop) (database createdb Jobs recreated every \~6s), but normal churn on a busy cluster can get there too.

How to spot it:

* `talosctl netstat -t -p -k` shows `1/init` holding a connection to [api.hetzner.cloud](<http://api.hetzner.cloud>)
* `talosctl logs controller-runtime | grep OperatorVIPConfig` shows `error getting server info: Limit of '3600' requests per hour`

What the BYO Talos docs should say:

* set `control_plane_private_vip_ipv4_enabled = false` (with `kube_api_load_balancer_enabled = true` for an HA internal endpoint), ideally before the cluster is bootstrapped, since it changes the cluster endpoint
* set `hcloud_csi_helm_values = { controller = { hcloudVolumeDefaultLocation = "<location>" } }`, otherwise the CSI controller needs the API to start and crashloops if it restarts while the budget is empty
* a rate-limited budget is per project, so rotating the token does not help

Switching a running cluster off the VIP is not free. The cluster endpoint feeds Talos's `--service-account-issuer` and `--api-audiences`, so every token already mounted in a pod gets rejected. On banano that cut Cilium off from the API (`kubernetes` Service lost its backends), Patroni demoted every Postgres to read-only, and Envoy Gateway, cert-manager and the operators crashlooped: 502s and a broken Unbind UI for about 20 minutes. Recovery was recreating every pod that talks to the API (Cilium first, then the Postgres pods, then all of `kube-system` and `unbind-system`). The docs should say to set this before bootstrap, and spell out the restart if someone changes it later.

issues.title: Redirect domain without a target port is saved but never routed
issues.description:
A domain added with a redirect and no `target_port` (API or MCP, the field doc says the port is ignored while a redirect is set) is saved on the service but left out of the Service CR. The domain gets no listener or route, so it 404s or fails TLS. The API answers 200 and get-service lists the domain, so nothing looks wrong.

`routableHosts` in apps/api/internal/repositories/service/runtime_config.go drops every host with a nil port before `ApplyRuntimeConfig` writes the spec. A redirect never reaches the service, so it does not need one, and the operator's `resolveHostPort` already falls back to the first service port.

Seen on banano with v0.1.101: moving [www.thebrownsboard.com](<http://www.thebrownsboard.com>) from the edge to the nodebb service as a 301 redirect. The edge released it, nodebb never claimed it in the cluster. Upserting it again with `target_port: 4567` fixed it.

Fix: keep redirect hosts in `routableHosts` whatever the port, or reject a host with neither a port nor a redirect at the API so it fails loudly.

issues.title: Domain changes restart the service, with downtime for services with a volume
issues.description:
Adding or removing a domain rolls the service out as a redeploy with a new deployment ID. The operator puts that ID on the pod template as the `unbind-deployment` label (apps/operator/internal/resourcebuilder/resourcebuilder.go `getCommonLabels`), so every replica is replaced even when nothing the pods run changed.

A service with a volume uses the Recreate strategy (deployment.go `buildDeploymentStrategy`), so it is down until the new pod is ready.

Seen on banano with v0.1.101:

* Moving [api.danklinux.com](<http://api.danklinux.com>) from the edge onto the dlx-docs-server service (1 replica, volume): about 40 seconds of 503 while the pod came back.
* Adding three redirect domains to nodebb restarted NodeBB three times. Rolling update, so no downtime, but a full restart for a redirect that never reaches the service.

Proposal: keep the deployment ID off the pod template (an annotation on the Deployment, or a label only on objects outside the template), and roll pods only when the pod spec changes. A redirect domain never changes the pod spec.

comments.body:
**Also seen 2026-10-14**

Adding domains to the five wban-apis redeployed each one. They have no volume, so they got a rolling update: about 30 s with two pods on the same hot wallets (UNB-400).

**After the change**

A domain change only touches routes. The wban-apis, NodeBB and dlx-docs-server keep running: no downtime on services with a volume, and no overlap on wallet services.

issues.title: Removing a domain briefly breaks the service's other domains
issues.description:
On Envoy Gateway, a service's listeners and HTTPRoutes are named by the domain's index: listener `https-<i>`, route `<svc>` for the first domain and `<svc>-<i>` after it (apps/operator/internal/resourcebuilder/networking/gateway.go, hostoptions.go `hostObjectName`). Removing a domain shifts every domain after it down one index, so their listeners and routes are rewritten in place for a different hostname. While the Gateway and the routes are updated one after another, those domains have a listener without a matching route.

Seen on banano with v0.1.101: the dux edge had [danklinux.com](<http://danklinux.com>), plugins., install., api. Removing [plugins.danklinux.com](<http://plugins.danklinux.com>) gave [install.danklinux.com](<http://install.danklinux.com>) 404 and [api.danklinux.com](<http://api.danklinux.com>) 503 for a few seconds, though neither was touched. The same happens when a domain is added in the middle with an overwrite.

Proposal: derive listener and route names from the hostname (sanitized, or a short hash) instead of the index, so removing one domain leaves the others' objects unchanged. Keep the first domain's route name for existing services if churn on upgrade matters.

issues.title: Several services on one domain, split by path
issues.description:
A domain belongs to one service. Item 5 of [UNB-375](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-375/domain-routing-redirects-basic-auth-headers-path-sharing-and-external), not in v0.1.101.

Still on an nginx edge on banano because of it:

* [appditto.com](<http://appditto.com>): `/` to the frontend, `/inquire` to the contact server
* [monkey.banano.cc](<http://monkey.banano.cc>): `/api` to monkey-server, `/` to monkey-frontend
* [boompow.banano.cc](<http://boompow.banano.cc>) after its cutover: `/graphql` and `/ws` (websocket) to the server, `/` to the frontend

Why: `CountHostConflicts` matches the host and ignores the path (apps/api/internal/services/service create.go, update.go, apply_staged_changes.go), and the gateway provider builds one listener per host per service (apps/operator/internal/resourcebuilder/networking/gateway.go).

Proposal: allow a domain on several services in a team when their paths differ. One HTTPS listener and certificate per domain, one HTTPRoute per service matched on its path prefix, longest prefix wins. The service with `/` owns the listener, or the listener moves to a shared per-domain Gateway. Redirect, basic auth and headers stay per route.

issues.title: Proxy a domain to a URL outside the cluster
issues.description:
No way to point a domain at an upstream outside the cluster. Item 6 of [UNB-375](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-375/domain-routing-redirects-basic-auth-headers-path-sharing-and-external), not in v0.1.101.

Still on an nginx edge on banano because of it: [install.danklinux.com](<http://install.danklinux.com>) proxies `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AvengeMedia/DankMaterialShell/master/core/install.sh` with TLS verification. Users run `curl ... | sh`, often without `-L`, so a redirect is not a substitute.

Proposal: a domain target that is an external URL: scheme, host, port and an optional path rewrite, TLS verified against the system CAs, upstream Host header set to the target. On Envoy Gateway: a `Backend` with an FQDN endpoint plus a `URLRewrite` filter (needs `extensionApis.enableBackend` in the EnvoyGateway config). Could be an "external" service type with no pods, so it gets domains like any other service.

issues.title: Path rules on a domain: redirects and fixed responses
issues.description:
v0.1.101 redirects a whole domain. Some sites need a rule for one path while the rest goes to the service.

Still on an nginx edge on banano because of it ([danklinux.com](<http://danklinux.com>)):

* `/blog/v1.2-release` 301 to `/blog/v1-2-release`, keeping the rest of the path and the query
* `/.well-known/org.flathub.VerifiedApps.txt` and `/.well-known/microsoft-identity-association.json` returned inline with a fixed body and content type

Both could also move into the docs app (a redirect route and two static files). Then [danklinux.com](<http://danklinux.com>) no longer needs the edge, only install. does.

Proposal: per-domain path rules matched on exact path or prefix:

* redirect: target URL, status, replace the matched prefix or the full path (Gateway API `RequestRedirect` with `ReplacePrefixMatch`)
* fixed response: status, content type, small body (Envoy Gateway `HTTPRouteFilter` `directResponse`)

issues.title: Route cleanup deletes Postgres credential secrets, databases lose their passwords
issues.description:
v0.1.101 added Secret to the route kinds (`RouteGVKs`, for basic auth htpasswd secrets). `cleanupStaleRoutes` lists every Secret labeled `app.kubernetes.io/instance=<service>` that the service controls and deletes the ones not in the desired route set. The Zalando credential secrets (`<role>.<cluster>.credentials.postgresql.acid.zalan.do`) carry that label and are controlled by the Unbind Service, and a database has no routes, so every database reconcile deletes all three of them.

The Postgres operator then recreates them with new random passwords it cannot apply (its own `postgres` password no longer matches), Unbind copies the new values into the service, and every app that restarts gets `password authentication failed for user "primarydb"`.

Seen on banano 2026-10-13: all 6 team Postgres lost their secrets at 19:06 UTC (operator start on v0.1.101), two again at 19:26 when they were reconciled. nodebb, umami, plausible and monkey-server crash looped until the role passwords were set to the new secret values by hand.

Fix (working tree): only treat a Secret as a route object when its name has the `-htpasswd` suffix the route builders use (`networking.IsRouteSecretName`), plus a regression test (`TestCleanupStaleRoutesKeepsNonRouteSecrets`).

After upgrading, clusters already hit need each role's password set to its secret value (`ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD` over the local socket), since the Postgres operator cannot log in to sync them.

issues.title: Deploy shows nothing when applying staged changes fails (e.g. domain already in use)
issues.description:
Clicking Deploy on staged changes spins and then does nothing when the apply request fails. The API answers 400 with a clear message, but the UI drops it.

Seen on banano 2026-10-13: adding [invoice.appditto.com](<http://invoice.appditto.com>) with basic auth to the invoice web service while the same host was still on the appditto edge service. `POST /staged-changes/apply` returned 400 four times (`hostConflictError`: `domain invoice.appditto.com already in use`). The user saw a spinner each time and no reason. It worked once the domain was removed from the edge.

Cause: in `apps/web/src/components/staged-changes/staged-changes-provider.tsx` the deploy mutation has `onError: () => endApplying(new Set())`. It clears the applying state and shows no toast or inline error.

Fix:

* Show the API error message on a failed apply (toast, and keep the changes staged).
* The dry run plan query likely hits the same error before Deploy is clicked. Surface plan errors in the staged changes panel too, so a conflicting domain is flagged before deploying.
* Nice to have: name the service that already holds the domain in the conflict message, so the user knows where to remove it.

issues.title: No way to move a service to another project or environment
issues.description:
A service can't be moved to another project or environment. `update-service` takes `project_id` and `environment_id` only to find the service.

Today the only way is to recreate it in the target: copy its config and variables, copy volume data by hand, remove each domain from the old service and add it to the new one, then delete the old service. References to the old service ID (`${{service:<id>.KEY}}`) have to be fixed by hand, and there is a short gap on each domain while the new one claims it.

The services of a team share one namespace, so a move within a team looks mostly like bookkeeping, not a rebuild. What it would touch:

* the service's environment in the database
* `ProjectRef`, `EnvironmentRef` and the `unbind-project` / `unbind-environment` labels the operator puts on everything it builds (`apps/operator/internal/resourcebuilder/resourcebuilder.go`)
* the `unbind-project` / `unbind-environment` labels on its PVCs, which volume listing filters on (`apps/api/internal/services/storage/pvc_read.go`), so its volume moves with it
* service groups: move the whole group, or take the service out of it
* variables: `${{project.KEY}}` and `${{environment.KEY}}` would resolve against the new scope. Check whether references between services in different projects are allowed, both from the moved service and to it
* name conflicts in the target environment
* permissions: editor on both the source and the target

Moving between teams is out of scope, since that changes the namespace.

Not checked yet: how much of the relabeling the operator reconciles on its own.

Came up moving the wallpaper service from its own project into danklinux on banano.

issues.title: Projects page: search, sort, manual ordering, favorites and a rows view
issues.description:
The Projects page is a flat grid of cards ordered by creation date. With 15+ projects in a team (banano has 16) it gets hard to scan and there is no way to shape the list.

Came up on Discord (Oct 13, 2026). Icons were also mentioned but are already covered by [UNB-258](https://linear.app/unbind/issue/UNB-258/we-can-let-people-pick-and-icon-for-projects-from-inside-the-services).

## What to add

* **Search**: filter the projects by name from the page itself. Keep the command palette (Ctrl+K) working as it does today.
* **Sort**: name, created date, last updated. Remember the choice per user.
* **Manual ordering**: drag to reorder projects. Ordering is one of the most-asked-for pieces here. The order needs to be stored on the API side (a display order on projects within a team) so it survives reloads and is shared across the team's members.
* **Favorites**: star a project so it shows up at the top of the list.
* **Rows view**: a toggle between the current card grid and a compact list of rows, one project per row. Same information as the card (name, environment and service counts, service icons).

## Notes

* `ProjectCardList` (`apps/web/src/components/team/project-card-list.tsx`) renders the grid. The list endpoint already accepts a sort order on created/updated date, see `apps/api/internal/repositories/project/queries.go`.
* Manual order and favorites need API and schema changes. Decide whether favorites are per user or per team before starting.
* Keep the docs in sync (`apps/docs`).

issues.title: Strip AI style from releases, workflows, UI text and docs (emojis, em dashes)
issues.description:
Generated text across the repo reads like AI output. Remove the emojis and em dashes and rewrite in plain sentences.

## Where

* Release notes: `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds the GitHub release body with emoji headings (`🚀 Unbind vX`, `📦 Container Images`, `🧰 Installer`, `📝 What's Changed`), 9 lines. Every published release since has them. Plain `##` headings instead, and decide whether to rewrite the existing release bodies.
* Workflow output: emojis in step names and echo lines in `build-app.yml` (3), `build-operator.yml` (3), `publish-charts.yml` (2), `ci.yml` (1).
* Scripts: `scripts/check-docs-data.sh`, `scripts/check-web-types.sh`.
* Em dashes, counted in lines: `apps/web/src` 31 (some user-facing UI copy), `README.md` 17, `apps/api` 14 (some in operation descriptions, which also become MCP tool descriptions), `deploy` 5, `.github` 2, `apps/installer` 2.
* Installer TUI uses ✓ / ✗ status glyphs (`apps/installer/internal/tui/view_common.go` and others). Those are status markers, probably keep.

## Rule going forward

No emojis and no em dashes in commits, release notes, workflow output, UI copy, API descriptions or docs. Use a comma, a period or parentheses. Worth a lint or CI grep so it does not come back.

issues.title: Redis: append-only file, on by default for new databases
issues.description:
Unbind Redis runs with `appendonly no` and the image's RDB save points (`3600 1 300 100 60 10000`). After a crash it comes back at the last snapshot, which can be minutes behind, or up to an hour when writes are slow. Apps that keep real state in Redis (BullMQ queues, balances; wban keeps user deposits and withdrawals there) lose writes. The old banano cluster ran wban's Redis with AOF everysec.

The CloudPirates chart has no AOF value, so it goes in through `extraFlags` / `extraConfig`. Simply turning it on is not safe: Redis started with `appendonly yes` over an existing `dump.rdb` and no AOF starts EMPTY. Checked with redis:8.10: 1000 keys, SAVE, restart with `--appendonly yes`, dbsize 0.

Both directions convert cleanly when Redis does it at runtime. Checked with redis:8.10:

* on: load the RDB, `CONFIG SET appendonly yes`, wait for the rewrite, kill, restart with `appendonly yes`. All keys there, including one written after the switch.
* off: AOF on, graceful stop, restart with `appendonly no`. All keys there.

Plan:

* `appendOnly` in the database config, Redis only. New Redis services get it on. Existing ones stay off until someone turns it on.
* An init container on the Redis pod converts the data on disk before Redis starts. When AOF is wanted and only an RDB exists, it loads the RDB in a private redis-server on a unix socket, turns AOF on and waits for the rewrite. When AOF is not wanted and an AOF exists, it loads the AOF, saves the RDB and removes the AOF directory. Restarts and toggles then never start from the wrong file.
* A toggle in the database settings, plus docs.
